To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
moderate levels of plasticity are optimal for driving evolutionary change, and that the evolution of plasticity itself may be driven by selection.
phenotypic plastic responses to novel environments can be an important source of adaptive evolution.

(i) moderate levels of phenotypically plastic traits may facilitate genetic evolution; (ii) high levels of phenotypical plasticity may reduce the likelihood of evolution; (iii) phenotypically plastic behaviours may drive evolution in novel directions by altering the selective pressures on morphology and physiology; and (iv) the effects of phenotypic change on evolution may be difficult to predict and require careful analysis of individual cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between phenotypic plastic response and genetic evolution in driving population differentiation and speciation.

phenotypic plastic response can be an important factor in stimulating genetic evolution.

plasticity is a key player in the evolutionary process, and that it is time that we took it seriously.
